title: Binary content that is neither bytes nor a string

source.note: composed: on the JSON wire binary content is a base64 string, so there is nothing to decode here and nothing the content could mean. It decodes as the object it is, and validate reports an Error: §5.1.4 requires the content to be represented as the format specifies, and Table 1 makes `binary` bytes.

notes: An Error, as for a non-string `text` content and on the same clause: §5.1.4 and §5.2.4 make the same demand of every format. The reading this case used to take — that a payload carried by reference is a shape the standard merely leaves undefined — does not survive §6.4, which does define how a large payload is referenced: a `control` request answered with a `control` message carrying a `structured`/`uri` submessage (case ecma-430/27). That is a different shape from a URL inside the content, so there is no reading under which this object is binary content. It still decodes, so a deployment that logs rather than rejects can see what arrived.
